scope: Theorem 8.2 (Four-dimensional boundary deformation) of the manuscript “Boundary graph deformations for the spacetime Penrose inequality” (preprints/Boundary-graph-deformations-for-the-spacetime-Penrose-inequality-September-27-2026/paper.pdf), one of the manuscripts of result family 260 of openai/math at commit 1581d4cbdd69. The statement is quoted verbatim from the text that pdftotext 24.02.0 (-raw -enc UTF-8) extracts from the PDF (SHA-256 4205f51d8f1b130b), with whitespace normalised, and was found there under this heading on PDF page 58. Text extraction flattens typeset mathematics (superscripts, subscripts, fractions, large operators, delimiters), so the quote can read differently from the typeset statement and can carry characters with no Unicode meaning; the PDF is authoritative. Finding the quote shows that the manuscript states it, not that it is true. AMVO has checked nothing about this claim.
statement: Let (M4, g, K) be smooth, connected and orientable, complete with its nonempty compact smooth boundary S included, with exactly one Euclidean coordinate end and compact complement. Suppose K is compactly supported. Let r be a smooth positive extension of the coordinate radius. Assume that, for some c0 > 0 and 0 < δ1 < 1, µ − |J|g ≥ c0r−4−δ1 on M, H + trS K < 0 on every component of S, with the normal into M. On the end assume g − δ = Oj(r−2 ) for every fixed j ≥ 0, Rg = O(r−4−δ1 ), and finite ADM energy in Equation (8.1). There is a smooth closed connected one-ended exterior Ω ⊂ M with nonempty compact boundary B ⊂ int M such that every full cut of B in Ω has g-area at least A∗. For every 0 < ϵ < 1 and all sufficiently large integers N there is a smooth metric b gϵ,N on Ω, complete with B included, satisfying Rb gϵ,N ≥ 0, Hb gϵ,N (B) < 0, b gϵ,N ≥ e−2ϵ g, (8.3) b gϵ,N − δ = O2(r−2 ), Rb gϵ,N = O(r−4−δ1 ), (8.4) Eb gϵ,N ≤ Eg + ΠN 3ω3 e−ϵN + e−ϵN/2 . (8.5) The boundary mean curvature uses the normal into Ω. The constant ΠN = C(1 + N)apol is polynomial in N, with C and apol depending only on the fixed data, ϵ and the fixed geometric choices. The constants in Equation (8.4) may depend arbitrarily on N.
